line_by_line_vs_hexagon_20.1.8: getLoopTripCount: 'Negated = TB != Header' plus getNegatedComparison before the swap. Same as Hexagon:649/695 minus predOpcodeHasNot; RISC-V branches have no negated-predicate form. Justified.

getComparisonKind/FromCC: BGEU/COND_GEU are now GEu (they were GEs, a real signed/unsigned bug). F009's COND_P_BEQIMM->EQ and COND_P_BNEIMM->NE labels are kept, and P_BEQIMM/P_BNEIMM stay in getComparisonKind. An immediate End from F015's p.bneimm/p.beqimm goes through the endIsImm path. It is materialised by getValueReg (ADDI x0,imm; simm5 fits) or compared as an imm in loopCountMayWrapOrUnderFlow (operand 1 is an imm, so no bogus swap).

imm/imm path: Hexagon:786-826 verbatim, except the 32-bit sign/zero normalisation by comparison signedness. Justified: checkForImmediate yields int64 from LUI/ADDI chains. A negative distance, or a wrong-direction/non-exact != loop, is declined, not miscounted (conservative for do/while first-fail constants).

loopCountMayWrapOrUnderFlow is only called for NE, and is skipped when a dominating branch proves Start!=End or a strict order. Hexagon calls it for every Cmp (its reason is Hexagon's endloop not decrementing at count<=1). On PULP a zero count is only possible for != (the ordered paths always give >=1 through the guard or proof), so this is justified. The port inside the function (checkForImmediate for End, the branch itself as the compare because RISC-V has no analyzeCompare, the TODO'd TBB!=MBB negation restored, operand 1 for the swap) is faithful. It is still Hexagon's inexact 'any unsigned >/!= use is a range check' heuristic, the same as upstream.

Register path: Hexagon's (Dist + (s-1) [+1]) >> log2 s is emitted as ((Dist-1)>>s)+1, or (Dist>>s)+1 for <=. This is equivalent mod 2^32 and does not overflow before a count of 2^32. The NE path is unchanged: Dist>>s, same instructions as before. The Swapped branch swaps start/end and their imm flags and CmpLess/CmpGreater, as 89adc2d4f93b does.

Guard: Hexagon's C2_cmpgti DistR,0 + C2_muxir becomes SLT/SLTU(First, End) [XORI 1 for <=], NEG, AND, ADDI 1, with First = Start+step, or End-step when swapped. Justified: RISC-V has no mux. It is also more precise than upstream: Hexagon's signed sign-test of DistR is wrong for unsigned distances >= 2^31 and for a first step that wraps, and Hexagon skips the check for unsigned start 0 even though End may be 0. isInt<12> bail-outs cover the ADDI immediates.

Omitting the guard when a dominating edge D->S (S has only D as predecessor and S dominates the preheader) establishes Start<End (<= for inclusive), with matching signedness, or when Start=ANDI End,mask with a != proof. This is not in Hexagon. It is sound: vregs are SSA, and the edge condition holds on every entry path. Sub-cases: signed ANDI needs a negative mask, and a signed proof is never accepted for an unsigned loop. The note explains it (keep the usual rotated-loop code unchanged).
checks.arithmetic_model: logs/20-F007-review/model.py: exact model of the emitted register-path arithmetic, including the guard, at 8-bit width, for every start/end pair, all 8 ordered predicates plus !=, and steps +-1/+-2/+-4. It is compared with a simulated do/while. 0 mismatches, excluding only IVs that run past the type's max/min, which is the note's stated 2^32 limit (UB for signed, endless for unsigned), and != with Start==End. This covers the width analogues of count 2^31, 2^32-1, INT_MIN/INT_MAX bounds and first-step wrap. model2.py: the unguarded formula under the proven relation has 0 mismatches in 779264 cases. A count of exactly 2^31 or 2^32-1 could not be simulated on GVSoC (billions of iterations), so this width-generic model is the evidence for those counts.

checks.runtime_guard_cost: When it is emitted: only for ordered (<,<=,>,>=) loops with a register bound and no dominating proof. The cost is +4 instructions (+5 for <=) of guard, plus ADDI -1/+1 for the ceil when that is needed, once per loop entry, in the preheader. Measured with benchmarks/gap9-sweep/runtime/run_runtime.py on a scratch copy, compilers base=build/int-20, mine=build/20-F007 and GAP9 GCC: 54/54 kernel/opt pairs run OK. Checksums match GCC. Cycles are identical base vs mine in all 54, and kernel .text disassembly is identical in all 54. The object SHA-256 values differ, but only outside .text (compiler ident). Example of the guard where it is not strictly needed: adv p_for, a guarded 'for (int *p=a+x; p<a+y; p++)' whose guard compares the indices, not the pointers, gets 6 extra preheader instructions (it was correct before too, because a pointer difference is a multiple of 4). This is a missed optimisation, not a bug, and none of the SDK kernels have it.
checks.declined_loops: Fresh fuzzer seeds 241-400 x O2/O3/Os/Oz, base=build/int-20, both simulated vs GAP9 GCC (logs/20-F007-review/fuzz/res.txt): 0 regressions. The only non-OK case is seed 330, a MISMATCH on both builds at all levels, including Oz with 0 hardware loops, so it is not hwloop related. lp.setup: 1699 -> 1698 in total. 7 compiles lose a loop (seeds 245, 288, 335). Attributed against b0f18c5: the loss is F007's, and it is the worker's pattern: an inner 'for (i<m)' inside an outer 'for (i0<(m&3))', where LLVM dropped the inner m>0 guard because it knows (m&3)!=0 implies m!=0. The loop is still correct as a branch loop (addi/bnez: 2 instructions per iteration). No SDK kernel is affected (identical text above). Unguarded do{}while(--u!=0) with an unknown u is rightly declined (u==0 means 2^32 iterations; a count-0 lp.setup would run once). I judge this not a regression that matters. It is recorded as a follow-up below.

warnings_checked: policy_check.py --repo wt/20-F007 --range b0f18c5a6b88..53aa20faf0b3 --stack-base llvmorg-20.1.8: 0 FAIL, 1 WARN, diff-size 561 lines. Accepted as one root cause. B01 (wrong direction/equality adjustment) and B02 (no zero/negative-trip handling) are two symptoms of one defect: when the fork copied Hexagon's computeCount, it left out the comparison-dependent part (Negated, AdjV/ceil, the wrap check, and later upstream's DistCheck). The guard is built into the count expression (Q & -Valid then +1, applied to the same ((Dist-1)>>s) value), so splitting it into two commits would leave an intermediate commit that still hangs on first-fail do/whiles. About 130 of the lines are the dominating-branch proof helpers (isRelationTrueOnEntry/isDistanceCheckedOnEntry). They exist only to avoid emitting that guard where it is provably redundant, so they belong to the same change.

Rule 12: CORE-V has no hardware-loop pass in LLVM 20; the note says so and uses HexagonHardwareLoops (the pass's origin) as the reference. Acceptable.
Rule 9 (new early returns): all are justified bail-outs that decline the hardware loop and leave a correct branch loop. The oracle, adversarial and fuzz runs show no wrong result.
findings_not_blocking: Follow-up (performance, P3): the dominating-proof matcher compares operands syntactically. (a) Guards on derived values, for example indices when the loop compares pointers, are not recognised, so a guarded pointer for-loop gets the 6-instruction guard (adv p_for). (b) Implied facts such as (m&3)!=0 => m!=0 are not recognised, so the 7 fuzzer loops above are declined. Neither is in the SDK kernels. Possible remedies: accept a proof on values related by a common affine map (ptr = base + idx<<k), or pass the IR-level trip count or guard facts down to the pass.

Inherited from Hexagon: loopCountMayWrapOrUnderFlow's heuristic ('the initial value is used in any unsigned >/!= branch, so assume a range check'; 'any non-COPY/PHI definition cannot wrap') is unsound in theory. A != loop whose start equals its end at run time (2^32-iteration source loop) could get count 0, which runs once. Before this change that case was never checked, so this is strictly more conservative than int-20.
